subject: GateRiver: IR runbook request and evidence handover
messages:
From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@gateriver.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.example
Date: 2027-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: IR runbook + SIG evidence transfer

Hi Maya,

Quick intro — I’m Jordan on GateRiver’s security team. We’re ramping for a SIG/SOC2 review and have a scheduled audit kickoff on 2027-07-25. During a routine review we saw an auth spike on 2027-07-09 that we want to validate as part of our controls testing.

Could you please provide: 
- Your Incident Response Plan (IR runbook) in a redacted PDF or DOCX
- SIG questionnaire evidence (control descriptions, sample logs)
- A small telemetry sample around 2027-07-09 (auth logs, session start/stop) — redacted is fine

Preferred delivery options: secure SFTP upload or a Google Drive link with limited access. We also need a short post-incident summary that states timeline and whether any customer data was affected.

Can you confirm who on your side will coordinate and an expected delivery date? Ideally we’d like artifacts by 2027-07-15 so our auditor has time to ingest.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Cole
Security Engineer, GateRiver
security@gateriver.com

(Attachment suggested: example SIG checklist — not required on initial ask)

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.example
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@gateriver.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2027-07-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IR runbook + SIG evidence transfer

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can meet the 2027-07-15 window with a few clarifications.

Short answers up front:
- Point of contact: me (maya) for coordination and delivery; karthik will handle log exports and redaction guidance; Marissa will route legal/PO or contract questions if needed.
- Delivery options: we prefer secure SFTP for telemetry samples and a limited Google Drive folder for policy artifacts (IRP, control mappings). We can also provide a zipped evidence bundle via Custody SFTP with a 7-day window.

Questions / notes:
1) For the telemetry sample, do you need raw Apache / auth logs or just token/auth events? Our standard sample includes: auth events, session creation, source IP, and masked user IDs.
2) Do you require a signed attestation or just a technical postmortem? If auditors require signatures we’ll land that via DocuSign.
3) Any specific SIG control IDs you want mapped first (e.g., A.9 / Access Control, A.12 / Logging)?

Proposed timeline:
- Today (11th): confirm delivery method and any required control mapping list
- 12th–13th: karthik pulls and redacts sample, Marissa prepares policy bundle and legal checklist
- 14th: internal review and packaging
- 15th: deliver evidence bundle to GateRiver SFTP and Drive link

I’ll start the SFTP request and share creds with a one-time passphrase when ready. If you want a short sync (15m) I’m available 11:30–12:00 PT.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.example

Attachment: (none yet)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.example
Cc: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@gateriver.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2027-07-11T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: IR runbook + SIG evidence transfer

Maya / Jordan — I pulled the minimal telemetry slice and performed redaction as discussed. Details below and included as an attachment stub.

What I pulled (telemetry_sample_20270710.tar.gz):
- auth_events.csv: time, event_type, source_ip, user_id_masked (last 4 chars visible), session_id
- app_logs.log: context lines surrounding auth failures (sanitized PII)
- kv_cache_access.csv: timestamps and shard ids (no customer content)

Redaction approach:
- User identifiers replaced with a consistent pseudonymization hash per user so auditors can follow sequences without seeing full identifiers.
- IP addresses: we provide /24 masked versions unless GateRiver needs full forensics; request requires justification.
- No requestor-supplied blobs or file contents were included.

Attached: telemetry_sample_20270710.tar.gz (archive, 3 files) — will upload to the SFTP once Maya confirms window and we have a recipient email for the transfer notification.

Note: We validated that the activity spike on 2027-07-09 was due to an automated client re-auth loop from a third-party integration; containment occurred on 2027-07-09 04:20 UTC by killing the integration token and rolling keys. No evidence of data exfiltration. I’ll include a short technical appendix in the postmortem.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.example

Attachment: telemetry_sample_20270710.tar.gz (attached)

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.example
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@gateriver.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2027-07-11T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Deliverable: IR playbook, SIG evidence map, telemetry sample, and postmortem

Jordan — delivering the artifacts per your request. See links and attached stubs below. Thanks for the quick coordination.

Deliverables included (package):
- IRP_GateRiver_Q2-2027.pdf (IR runbook, redacted operational contact info) — Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Gx_fake_drive_link
- SIG_evidence_mapping.xlsx (control-to-evidence map) — Drive link in folder
- telemetry_sample_20270710.tar.gz (SFTP upload completed, notification sent to security@gateriver.com)
- postmortem_summary_20270711.txt (short timeline + root cause + remediation) — attached below

Post-incident summary (excerpt):
- Timeline: 2027-07-09 02:43 UTC — auth spike detected by monitoring; 02:55 UTC — automated mitigation throttled requests; 04:20 UTC — integration token revoked and keys rotated; 04:40 UTC — anomaly ceased.
- Root cause: misconfigured third-party integration creating auth retry loop.
- Impact: transient availability impact for a subset of customers; no customer PII or raw data accessed or exfiltrated per forensic checks.
- Remediation: token rotation, added rate-limiting and integration validation tests; scheduled a follow-up tabletop on 2027-07-20.

We’ve included a limited set of logs for auditor consumption; if you need additional fields (full IPs, raw session payloads) please let us know and provide a signed request and scope for redaction.

If GateRiver’s auditor needs a signed attestation I can route the DocuSign to our Security Director, Marissa Cole, and we’ll return a signed attestation within 48 hours.

Regards,
Maya Srinivasan
Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.example

Attachments: IRP_GateRiver_Q2-2027.pdf (pdf), postmortem_summary_20270711.txt (txt)
